documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53F establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

RA: seropositive, diagnosed 2014 by an outside rheumatology group, who still see her about every 4-6 months. Methotrexate 20 mg every Sunday plus prednisone 5 mg each morning and folic acid on the other six days. Says the joints are "mostly behaving" - stiff for a while on waking, hands worst. Had both carpal tunnels released in 2016.

Blood counts: this spring hematology worked up her low white count and enlarged spleen - marrow biopsy in April, a needle sample of the spleen in May, both reportedly without anything malignant. Told it is Felty syndrome. Keeps filgrastim syringes at home and injects only when hematology calls with an ANC under 1000; has used it maybe twice. No infections this year.

Bones: DXA in 2019 showed osteoporosis, blamed on years of prednisone. Risedronate weekly since, calcium/D twice a day. No fractures.

Fatigue: carries a chronic fatigue diagnosis from her old office going back to roughly 2017. Cut her library hours because of it, now on disability. Sleeps 8 hours and still wakes tired. Mood ok.

Allergies: Bactrim - throat closed, ambulance (anaphylaxis). Ibuprofen - gastritis, told never to take NSAIDs.
FHx: mother RA. Maternal aunt lupus. Father T2DM and HTN.
SHx: never smoked, no alcohol since starting methotrexate. Lives alone. Part-time at a public library.

Exam: well-appearing, thin. Vitals as recorded. HEENT unremarkable, no oral ulcers. No cervical or axillary nodes. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable below the left costal margin, nontender. Hands: MCP prominence and mild ulnar drift bilaterally, well-healed carpal tunnel scars, no warm or boggy joints today. No edema. Skin without rash or bruising.

A/P:
1. Seropositive RA - per rheumatology; will draw monitoring labs here when it helps her.
2. Felty syndrome - per hematology. CBC today for our own baseline.
3. Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis - continue risedronate and calcium/D; vitamin D level today. We will refill these.
4. Chronic fatigue syndrome - longstanding, pacing her activity.
5. Health maintenance - HCV and HIV screens today. Colonoscopy 2018 per her report, will confirm in records. Flu shot and pneumococcal vaccine next month. No live vaccines on her regimen.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Patricia - your labs from Tuesday are back. White count and neutrophils are low, about where your hematology notes say they usually run, and your hemoglobin is mildly low as before. Kidney and liver tests, which matter on methotrexate, are normal. Vitamin D is fine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. I'll keep an eye on the trend along with your hematologist.

reports.text: Outside report, received 9/28/2021. Specimen: bone marrow core biopsy and aspirate, right posterior iliac crest. Core biopsy adequate. Cellularity is reduced for age. Myeloid series present with paucity of mature forms beyond the myelocyte stage, consistent with maturation arrest. Erythroid and megakaryocytic lineages present without dysplasia. No increase in blasts. No lymphoid aggregates or infiltrating process. Iron stores present.
reports.conclusion: Hypocellular marrow with myeloid maturation arrest. No evidence of malignancy.

reports.text: Outside report, received 9/28/2021. Specimen: fine-needle aspiration, spleen, ultrasound guided. Smears show a mixed population of small lymphocytes, scattered histiocytes and blood elements. No monoclonal population on flow cytometry. No granulomas. No malignant cells.

Visit date: 11/04/2021

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for taking over primary care for Ms. Kelleher, whom we follow for seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, diagnosed here in 2014 with strongly positive RF and anti-CCP and a synovial biopsy at the time showing pannus with plasma cell and lymphocyte infiltrates. Her course has been complicated by Felty syndrome, which hematology is managing.

Today she has about 45 minutes of morning stiffness. Exam shows fixed MCP changes in both hands without active synovitis; wrists and knees quiet.

Medications: methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily except methotrexate day, risedronate 35 mg weekly, calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 twice daily, filgrastim 300 mcg as needed.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Plan: continue current regimen. CBC and CMP every 3 months; happy for these to be drawn at your office and copied to us. Return in 6 months.

Sincerely,
Rheumatology

documents.title: Hematology Consultation Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Date of service: 12/30/2024

Re: Patricia Kelleher, DOB 04/18/1968

Ms. Kelleher, 56, is seen for scheduled Felty syndrome follow-up, with your November note and CBC in hand. For the last two to three months she has felt more worn down than usual. Her mornings have changed: stiffness now lasts beyond an hour, and the small joints of both hands and the wrists swell. No fevers, infections, bleeding or weight change.

History: seropositive RA since 2014; the rheumatology synovial biopsy at diagnosis showed pannus with plasma cells and lymphocytes. Felty syndrome since 2021 (marrow hypocellular with maturation arrest; splenic aspirate benign). Glucocorticoid-related osteoporosis. Chronic fatigue syndrome. Bilateral carpal tunnel release 2016.
Medications: methotrexate 20 mg weekly; prednisone 5 mg each morning; folic acid 1 mg except methotrexate day; risedronate 35 mg weekly; calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 600 mg/400 IU twice daily; filgrastim 300 mcg SC as needed for ANC <1000.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).
Family history: mother RA; maternal aunt SLE; father type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, part-time library work.

Exam: soft tissue swelling over MCPs and wrists bilaterally. Spleen palpable below the costal margin.

Data: hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL. Serum iron 38 mcg/dL (low), ferritin 140 ng/mL (normal). ESR 46 mm/h, CRP 34 mg/L. RF and anti-CCP positive. White count and ANC at her baseline.

Impression: the fall in hemoglobin fits anemia of chronic inflammation - low circulating iron with preserved stores, in the setting of increased RA activity. Inflammatory signaling sequesters iron; iron supplementation would not be expected to help. Neutropenia stable.

Recommendations: the anemia should follow control of the arthritis; I have asked her to see rheumatology promptly about the joint symptoms. No iron. Continue filgrastim as needed. CBC in 6 months.

Hematology & Oncology

Texted this morning about a red sore patch on her right shin since Sunday; seen same day.

No injury she remembers, dry skin from the cold. Area warm and tender, spreading a little since yesterday. No chills. Not using filgrastim lately.

Exam: vitals as charted. Right anterior lower leg with a blanching, warm, tender area of erythema about 8 x 6 cm, margins marked with pen. No fluctuance, no drainage, no streaking. No inguinal nodes. Calf soft. Left leg normal.

CBC today: WBC 2.3, ANC 0.9.

A/P: nonpurulent cellulitis, right lower leg, in a neutropenic patient on methotrexate and prednisone.
- Cephalexin 500 mg four times daily x 7 days. Sulfa antibiotics excluded (anaphylaxis).
- ANC under 1000: called hematology - they advise she use her filgrastim per her standing instructions; she has syringes at home.
- Elevate, moisturize the skin.
- If the redness passes the pen line, or fever, call immediately - low threshold for ED.
Phone check in 48 hours.

documents.title: Same-day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called at 8 with three days of cough and feeling feverish; seen this morning.

Cough productive, tired, some right-sided chest discomfort with deep breaths. Felt hot overnight. No hemoptysis. Third infection this year after the two leg cellulitis episodes (January here, March at an urgent care).

Exam: vitals as charted, not in distress, speaking full sentences. Crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart regular. Leg skin healed bilaterally.

CXR done in house: right lower lobe consolidation (see report). CBC: WBC 2.5, ANC 1.1.

A/P:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, RLL, outpatient-treatable today (oxygenating well, eating and drinking, has support by phone). Levofloxacin 750 mg daily x 5 days - she is sulfa-anaphylactic; reviewed tendon precautions with the prednisone. Call or go to the ED for breathlessness, confusion, or not improving in 48-72 hours.
2. Recurrent infections with Felty neutropenia - three in four months. Referral to hematology for an earlier visit than the routine summer one; note sent.
3. Left leg cellulitis from March resolved.
RN check-in Monday. Recheck visit in about 6 weeks.

Exam: afebrile, sat normal on room air. Lungs clear throughout, including the right base. Spleen tip palpable.

A/P: pneumonia resolved clinically; no repeat film needed at this point. Hematology 7/20 for recurrent infections. Low threshold to be seen for any fever. Next routine visit late summer.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Admission 06/14/2026 - Discharge 06/16/2026
Service: Internal Medicine

Reason for admission: evaluation of repeated infections in a neutropenic patient.

History: 58-year-old woman with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and Felty syndrome (chronic neutropenia, splenomegaly). Over the past half year she has had two episodes of lower-leg cellulitis (January, March) and a right lower lobe pneumonia in April, each treated as an outpatient. She presented through the emergency department for evaluation of this pattern. Her arthritis is currently quiet on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone.

PMH: as above; glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis; chronic fatigue syndrome. PSH: bilateral carpal tunnel release; bone marrow biopsy and splenic aspiration 2021.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Exam on admission: afebrile, BP 130/80, HR 78, RR 16. No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Joints without synovitis; chronic deformities of longstanding RA in the hands. Palpable spleen tip. Skin intact, no cellulitis.

Data: Hgb 12.5, WBC 2.1, ANC 0.8, platelets 180. RF positive, ACPA positive. CMP unremarkable. Blood cultures x2: no growth. CXR: clear, prior RLL opacity resolved.

Hospital course: no active infection identified. Hematology consulted; filgrastim 300 mcg given on 6/14 and 6/15 with ANC 1.9 (WBC 3.4) on 6/16. Given the frequency of infections on as-needed dosing, hematology recommended scheduled filgrastim twice weekly. Rheumatology aware; no change to methotrexate or prednisone.

Discharge medications:
- Filgrastim 300 mcg SC twice weekly (Mon/Thu) - CHANGED from as needed
- Methotrexate 20 mg weekly
- Prednisone 5 mg daily
- Folic acid 1 mg daily except methotrexate day
- Risedronate 35 mg weekly
- Calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 600 mg/400 IU twice daily

Follow-up: PCP within one week; hematology 7/20 as scheduled. Return for temperature 38.0 C or higher.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know she was in the hospital Sunday to Tuesday. Went in through the ED Sunday afternoon because she was worried about all the infections. Told no infection right now; they gave her filgrastim shots and her count came up, and she is to take it twice a week now instead of only when called. No discharge papers sent to us yet - requested. Feels fine, afebrile. Has syringes; specialty pharmacy shipping more. Post-hospital visit booked Monday 6/22.

documents.body:
Hospital 6/14-6/16 for evaluation of recurrent infections; summary not received yet, history from patient and her discharge med sheet.

Per patient: no infection found, cultures negative so far, chest film clear. Got filgrastim two days and her neutrophils rose. Discharged on filgrastim twice weekly (Mon/Thu). Gave herself this morning's dose without trouble. No fevers.

Med reconciliation: filgrastim changed from as-needed to 300 mcg twice weekly - list updated. Methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg, folic acid, risedronate, calcium/D unchanged.

Exam: afebrile, well. Lungs clear. Spleen tip palpable. Skin intact on both legs.

A/P: Felty syndrome with recurrent infections, now on scheduled growth factor. Hematology 7/20. No NSAIDs. Fever 100.4 or higher: call us any hour. Follow-up late summer.

documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Seen 07/20/2026.

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Kelleher after her June admission. Since discharge she has had no fevers or infections. She is injecting filgrastim 300 mcg Mondays and Thursdays without difficulty.

Exam: well-appearing. Spleen tip palpable. No adenopathy. Skin intact.
CBC: WBC 2.9, ANC 1.4, hemoglobin 12.3, platelets 175.
Medications: filgrastim 300 mcg SC twice weekly; methotrexate 20 mg weekly; prednisone 5 mg daily; folic acid; risedronate 35 mg weekly; calcium/vitamin D3.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Assessment: Felty syndrome with improved neutrophil count on scheduled filgrastim.
Plan: continue twice-weekly filgrastim. CBC with differential in one month - fine to draw at your office and send to us. I will see her again in three months.
